title: Gandhara's Relationship with Hastinapur
body:
Gandhara's Relationship with Hastinapur

To strengthen Hastinapur's political alliances, Bheeshma negotiated the marriage of Dhritarashtra with Gandhari, the princess of Gandhara. When Gandhari learned that her husband-to-be was born blind, she made a supreme vow of dedication: she wrapped her face with a napkin, voluntarily blindfolding herself for life so as not to enjoy any pleasure that her husband was denied.
This marriage, however, carried seeds of deep geopolitical and familial resentment. Gandhari's brother, Shakuni, harboured a silent, unyielding hatred toward Bheeshma and the Kuru dynasty. According to ancestral accounts, the Kurus had conquered Gandhara, imprisoned King Subala and his sons, and subjected them to slow starvation by feeding them only a single grain of rice each day.
Subala chose his youngest son, Shakuni, to survive, forcing his other sons to sacrifice their grains to him so that he could become the instrument of Gandhara's revenge. Shakuni's father broke Shakuni's ankle before his death, ensuring he would never forget the cruelty of Hastinapur. Using dice made from his father's bones, which obeyed his every command, Shakuni established himself in the Kuru court as Duryodhana's evil genius, dedicating his life to the absolute destruction of the Bharata race.
